clue.text: Churchman may be best in prayer

indicators.note: the letters of the following words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A clergyman could well be at his finest when he is praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is the anagram signal, rearranging the twelve letters of BEST IN PRAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Calvinist church governed by elders is a churchman of that denomination.

clue.text: Criticize girl who found hope at last

parts.note: to pan is to criticize harshly
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a girl who finally discovered optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the first woman opened the forbidden box, releasing evils; hope alone remained at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical woman whose box left hope inside after all evils escaped.

clue.text: Yoga has half Mexico in a whirl with this marriage custom

indicators.note: spun round in a whirl, the letters are mixed up
half of the word Mexico, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A yoga class in Mexico spins round a wedding tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes MEX from Mexico; 'in a whirl' rearranges YOGA plus MEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom of marrying outside one's own tribe or group.

clue.text: Whence the current bombardments

definitions.meaning: the source from which an electric current comes
a battery is a sustained attack, as by artillery

explanation.surface: Where the flow comes from in a heavy shelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a river or the present, but it is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric cells supply current, and artillery fire or assaults are a sense of the same word.

clue.text: Initially, the Red Ensign is on the ship in the lock

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: The Red Ensign flag flies on the ship while it is in a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign is the flag of the British merchant navy. 'lock' looks like a canal lock but is hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl or long lock of hair.

clue.text: Top palindrome ?

indicators.note: the wordplay is just that the word reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is the spinning toy: something that rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is something that turns round, a revolving thing.

clue.text: Venetian ice-cream vendor

definitions.meaning: the merchant of Venice in Shakespeare's play
a stock Italian name once typical of ice-cream sellers

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's merchant of Venice bears this name, and it was the stereotypical name of an Italian ice-cream seller in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Italian first name, borne by Shakespeare's merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Party man, unfortunate fellow, gets the bird

parts.note: a whip enforces discipline in a political party
poor means unlucky
Will, a man's name

explanation.surface: A party member and a hapless chap are jeered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' sounds like being booed, but the answer is a North American nightjar.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American nightjar named after its call is a bird.

clue.text: Striker gives information to the Press

definitions.meaning: a worker (hand) who is out on strike

explanation.surface: A worker on strike passes a statement to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: A HAND is a worker and OUT means on strike, so a striker is a hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: An issued press release is a common sense; the striker reading splits it into worker plus strike.

clue.text: Lands in New Jersey and Delaware, for instance

definitions.text: Lands in New Jersey and Delaware, for instance

parts.words: Lands in New Jersey and Delaware, for instance
parts.note: property lands, read also as E (eastern) plus a word for New Jersey and Delaware, which are American states

explanation.surface: Someone buys property along the American east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: New Jersey and Delaware are Eastern states, so E (east) before the word for such members of the union gives the word for landed properties.
explanation.definitionFit: Large landed properties in the country are called by this name.

clue.text: Adequate story about a fact is garbled

indicators.note: garbled words are jumbled, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An acceptable tale that gets the facts muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garbled' rearranges STORY and A FACT IS; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Good enough to meet requirements, sufficient.

clue.text: Post-mortem requirement when one is 17

parts.note: 17 down's clue is 'with a will': someone who dies having made a will needs that will proved in court

explanation.surface: A forensic note about what is needed after an autopsy on a seventeen-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post-mortem' suggests an autopsy, but it means simply after death; 17 refers to 17 down, which defines a person who has made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Official proving of a dead person's will is required before the executors can act.

clue.text: Material difference in taste

indicators.note: a difference made to the following words signals rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Fabric that marks a contrast in someone's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difference' acts as the anagram signal on IN TASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin glossy fabric imitating satin is a dress material.

clue.text: Zero change in a flower perhaps

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
to change is to vary

explanation.surface: A botanist notices no alteration at all in a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 'er'; the page prints 'in a flower perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed-bearing organ of a plant sits at the base of the pistil inside a bloom.

clue.text: Domineering and wicked without hesitation

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: impious means irreverent, wicked
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A bully who is evil and never pauses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of outside, so the hesitation sits within the word for wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogantly commanding behaviour is domineering.

clue.text: Affirm forecast about a point

indicators.note: one word goes about, around, another

parts.note: to predict is to forecast
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A forecaster asserts a prediction about a particular point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside PREDICT; 'point' is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or declare something as true is to affirm it.

clue.text: Turned up secret Rousseau extract

indicators.note: an extract is a passage taken out of the words secret Rousseau

explanation.surface: A secret excerpt from Rousseau has been discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' seems to mean discovered, but it is the definition of a nose turned up at the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a nose tilted upward at the end, as in a snub nose.

clue.text: One of 9 follows troop-leader with a will

indicators.note: the leader of troop is its first letter

parts.note: one of the lands of 9 across, a single landed property

explanation.surface: A soldier follows the leader of a troop with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' looks like 'eagerly' but means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies leaving a valid will is described this way.

clue.text: What we do to opponents when we are five-love perhaps

definitions.text: What we do to opponents when we are five-love perhaps

parts.words: What we do to opponents when we are five-love perhaps
parts.note: leading five games to love, a team dominates and intimidates its rivals

explanation.surface: A tennis player describes the effect of a commanding lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Five-love is a tennis score: five games to nil, a lead that intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate or daunt someone with a display of power.

clue.text: Coffee or port ?

definitions.meaning: a fine coffee, originally shipped from Arabia
a Red Sea harbour town in Yemen

explanation.walkthrough: The coffee takes its name from the Yemeni port it was exported through.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yemeni harbour gave its name to the Arabian coffee shipped from it.

clue.text: A post under military intelligence ? That's wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A job in the intelligence service that turns out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job but is a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: An error or a wrong done is a blunder.

clue.text: After tea let us build some huts

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
let's is the contraction of let us

explanation.surface: After tea, a group decides to build cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR misread 'let' as 'J'; 'build some' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden Swiss-style cottages or holiday cabins are kinds of huts.

clue.text: Examine wasp, for instance, including its tail

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a wasp is an example of an insect
the tail of the wasp is its last letter, P

explanation.surface: Look closely at a wasp, sting end and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the wasp: its last letter P goes inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise something closely is to examine it.

clue.text: The measure of crime

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot, a measure

explanation.surface: How the scale of an offence is gauged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a crime.

clue.text: This month, worker is on short time

parts.note: inst. is the old commercial abbreviation for 'of this month'
a worker ant

explanation.surface: This month an employee works shorter hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short time' looks like reduced hours but is the definition, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment or very brief period is a short time.

clue.text: Hence the drying-up of a lake for example? Could be

definitions.text: Hence the drying-up of a lake for example? Could be

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A geography question about why a lake dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges A LAKE plus EG; the whole clue also describes how water seeping away empties a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Water escaping through a hole is a cause of a reservoir running dry.

clue.text: A friend at the City whose services are free

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Ur of the Chaldees, the ancient city in the Bible

explanation.surface: A chum working in London's financial district who does not charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial district, but it is UR, the ancient Mesopotamian city; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional performs without pay, so someone whose services are free.

clue.text: Like the oil in the widow's cruse, for all that

definitions.text: Like the oil in the widow's cruse
definitions.meaning: the widow's cruse in the Bible (1 Kings 17) never ran short of oil, so its oil was never any smaller
in spite of that, all the same

explanation.surface: A biblical image of endless supply, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added stray characters at the end; the page ends 'for all that'. Read as three words, the answer describes oil that never diminished.
explanation.definitionFit: However or all the same is the sense of for all that.
